transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me a little bit about what has been bothering you lately and what brings you to see me today?

I've been really struggling with eating out of control and consuming huge amounts of food lately. Once I start eating, I feel like I just can't stop myself. This has been going on for about two and a half years now, and I really don't know what to do anymore.

After these episodes of eating large amounts of food, do you ever engage in any behaviors to try to prevent weight gain, such as self-induced vomiting, excessive exercising, or the misuse of laxatives?
Yes, I feel so guilty afterward that I force myself to throw up. I also use laxatives and try to fast or exercise excessively the next day to make sure I don't gain weight.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were [Binge-Eating Disorder, Bulimia Nervosa]. Based on the patient's report of regular compensatory behaviors such as self-induced vomiting, laxative misuse, and excessive exercise to prevent weight gain, the diagnosis of Binge-Eating Disorder is ruled out, and Bulimia Nervosa is confirmed.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports recurrent episodes of binge eating accompanied by a lack of control, followed by inappropriate compensatory behaviors (self-induced vomiting, laxative misuse, fasting, and excessive exercise) to prevent weight gain, meeting the DSM-5 criteria for Bulimia Nervosa.
